assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation is a genuine game-changer: a simple chemical idea (a bifunctional molecule that recruits an E3 ligase to a target) that opened an entirely new drug modality and now has clinical consequences. Molecular glue degraders, linked to the thalidomide mechanism, add a second, mechanistically clear strand.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the first PROTACs; Ciulli provided the structural/VHL-ligand basis that made the approach drug-like. Handa, Ito and others clarified the cereblon glue mechanism, so a three-person limit leaves real allocation trade-offs.
assessment.maturity: Multiple degraders are in advanced clinical trials and the mechanism is independently confirmed; recognition is timely though approval-level clinical proof is still arriving.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or also include molecular glues (cereblon) given the three-laureate limit.
I have not independently verified the current clinical-approval status of degraders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells build proteins with new chemistry. It is original, conceptually clean, and widely used as a tool in biology, protein engineering and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pairs in living cells; Chin extended the approach to eukaryotes and multi-site and quadruplet-codon reprogramming. Yokoyama and Mehl are also credited, so priority questions remain.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent use; mature and stable, arguably somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Exact priority split between Schultz/Wang and Chin.
Chemistry versus biology framing of the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one nucleotide to another without double-strand breaks, a precise chemical solution that is new and already in clinical trials. It is an elegant, simple route to programmable genome chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab developed cytosine (Komor) and adenine (Gaudelli) base editors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related deaminase-based approach, so the supplied credit is contestable beyond Liu.
assessment.maturity: Very fast adoption, with early human clinical data; arguably early for a full retrospective but the impact is already evident.
uncertainties: Whether Liu alone, or Liu with trainees, is the proper attribution; the Nishida/Kondo parallel work complicates priority.
Overlap with prime editing, which could favour a combined Liu recognition.
Long-term clinical safety evidence is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned potentials give near quantum-mechanical accuracy at force-field cost, transforming what simulation can reach in materials and molecular chemistry. This is a real step change for my own field, and it is quantitatively validated against first-principles data.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello introduced neural-network potentials, Csányi and Bartók the Gaussian approximation potentials; Parrinello's broader Car-Parrinello and metadynamics legacy may make him a natural anchor. Other credited names (von Lilienfeld, E) are also important.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing; transferability, long-range physics and biomolecular applicability are still developing, so the timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Reliability and generalisation of ML potentials outside training data.
How to weigh the contribution of the many groups in a fast-moving field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based computational catalyst design (d-band model, scaling relations) gives a simple, predictive picture connecting theory quantitatively to experiment, with experimentally validated catalysts. This matches my standard of simple ideas with real consequences.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the clear central figure; Mavrikakis and Rossmeisl contributed key extensions (surface reactivity trends, electrocatalysis). Scheffler and Jaramillo are less central.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental validation, though the scaling-relation limits are an active topic.
uncertainties: How far the descriptors have truly produced industrially deployed catalysts.
Priority relative to earlier work by Hammer/Nørskov and others not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates by liquid-liquid phase separation are a completely new organising principle in cells with broad consequences, and physical-chemical in nature.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquid droplets; Rosen demonstrated multivalent phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag supplied key theory and sequence grammar.
assessment.maturity: Field is young and contested regarding physiological relevance and the liquid-state interpretation; recognition is perhaps premature.
uncertainties: Debate on whether many condensates are truly phase-separated in vivo.
Possible fit with the physiology/medicine prize rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled delivery of siRNA and mRNA drugs and vaccines, with clear, large real-world consequences. The chemistry of pH-dependent ionizable lipids is simple and decisive.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues built the formulation and ionizable-lipid basis; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan contributed lipid design and delivery. Credit is spread across academic and company groups.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated by COVID-19 vaccines and approved siRNA drugs, so impact is established.
uncertainties: Hard attribution among many contributors and with industry.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory resolved the Levinthal paradox and gave a quantitative framework for folding, linking simulation and experiment, close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic developed funnel theory; Dill the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model foundations; Fersht the experimental mapping. Credit among theorists is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Long established, though practical impact now overlaps with structure prediction, which has already been recognised.
uncertainties: Whether the theory is judged a 'game-changer' relative to AlphaFold-era prediction.
Allocation of credit between Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Fersht.
